title: When someone you care about is away or at risk
summary: Coping with worry when a colleague, friend or family member is away, for example on reserve duty or deployed.
body: Worry about someone who is away can sit in the background all day. This is a normal response, not a weakness.
Some things that help: keeping a small routine, deciding when you will check for news rather than checking all day, and sharing how you feel with one person you trust.
If you are also covering their work, it is fine to feel stretched and worried at the same time. Tell your manager if the combination is becoming hard.
If worry is affecting your sleep or daily life, your employee assistance programme or a health professional can help.
